purpose: find vulnerabilities that only appear in a running application by sending hostile requests to an authorized non-production target
entry_criteria: Written scope names the target URLs, environment and test window
Target is non-production or has explicit owner approval for testing
Test accounts and data exist; no real customer data is used
inputs: target base URL and API definition
procedure: Confirm scope and window in writing; verify the target host matches the approved list before sending any traffic.
Run an authenticated crawl or API-definition-driven scan per role, with rate limits agreed with the environment owner.
Triage each alert; reproduce with a minimal request and record request and response evidence.
Rate by exploitability and data exposure; open fix issues with owner and SLA.
Retest each fixed issue with the same request and confirm the behavior changed.
Report coverage honestly: which routes and roles were and were not exercised.
deliverables: scan report with raw requests and responses
acceptance_criteria: Scan stayed inside the approved scope
Each reported issue has a reproduction
No open critical or high finding without an approved exception
Coverage gaps are listed, not hidden
validation_method: Independent retest of fixed findings with the original request.

validation.command: zap-api-scan.py -t $API_SPEC_URL -f openapi -r reports/dast.html -J reports/dast.json   # example; non-production target only
validation.expect: report generated; no high alerts outside the approved baseline
every host listed is in the approved scope file

failure_modes.detection: Request log contains a host not in scope
failure_modes.response: Stop immediately; notify the environment owner; record an incident note

failure_modes.detection: Coverage statement lists no authenticated routes
failure_modes.response: Mark INCONCLUSIVE; rerun with role accounts

failure_modes.detection: Error rate rises during the window
failure_modes.response: Lower the rate limit and rerun in the next window

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: An authenticated scan of a staging API finds that changing an order id in the URL returns another user's order. Reproduced with two test accounts, rated high, fixed with an ownership check, retested with the same request returning 403.
